news.title: Körber: AI investment is up, but 3 in 4 leaders say decision-making is now more complex
news.summary: A Körber survey of 2,000 senior decision-makers in the U.S. and Germany finds that firms running AI across the enterprise perform better than those still piloting it, even though both groups spend on AI decision support at about the same rate.
news.why: Buyers and supply chain managers should weigh process readiness, data quality and clear decision ownership alongside AI spending when judging vendor promises of returns.

news.title: Diesel prices punished shippers in September, FTR says
news.summary: FTR's Shippers Conditions Index fell to -17.3 in September as record diesel prices and weak capacity conditions made the U.S. truckload market one of the hardest months for shippers since 2022, and FTR expects a tougher outlook than it previously forecast.
news.why: Shippers should expect elevated truckload rates and fuel surcharges to persist and should build fuel-price contingencies into their freight budgets and carrier contracts.

news.title: Small businesses upbeat about holiday peak
news.summary: A DHL Express survey of more than 400 small and mid-sized business leaders shows most expect steady or higher holiday sales, while tariffs and trade policy are seen as the top headwind.
news.why: Importers at smaller firms should plan holiday inventory and customs paperwork early, since tariffs and delivery delays are the most cited risks to peak-season timing.

news.title: Shipping Industry Presses for Global IMO Climate Deal as Divisions Over Rules Persist
news.summary: Nine major shipping associations are asking governments to agree on global greenhouse gas rules, arguing that the current uncertainty is holding back investment in cleaner ships and alternative fuels.
news.why: Cargo owners and carriers face possible future fuel and surcharge changes under global shipping emissions rules, so they should watch the IMO negotiations when planning long-term contracts.

news.title: U.S. Targets Ship-to-Ship Transfers in Expanded Iran Maritime Blockade
news.summary: U.S. Central Command says it will treat vessels that receive cargo at sea from ships loaded in Iran as trying to evade its blockade of Iranian ports and may act against them.
news.why: Traders and charterers handling petroleum or other cargo in the region face higher sanctions and seizure risk, so they should run enhanced counterparty and cargo-origin checks before accepting any at-sea transfers.

news.title: More U.S. LNG Cargoes Divert to Europe in Relief for Tight Market
news.summary: Several U.S. liquefied natural gas tankers have recently been rerouted toward Europe, easing supply in a tight market and putting downward pressure on prices.
news.why: Buyers in Asia and other non-European markets may face tighter LNG availability and higher spot prices, so they should review supply commitments and alternative sourcing.

news.title: Trump Unveils $17 billion of Southeast Asia Deals for U.S. firms, White House Says
news.summary: The White House says more than $17 billion in U.S. commercial deals and investments were announced across Southeast Asia, including a large aircraft sale and defense financing.
news.why: Buyers sourcing aircraft, energy, defense or data-center equipment should watch for new U.S.-linked supply options in the region, though headline deal values often take months to become binding orders.

news.title: Report: Asia-North America Trade Lane Presents High Risk Level
news.summary: WiseTech Global's four-week outlook rates overall ocean risk on Asia to North America lanes as high, citing tightening capacity, weak booking acceptance and poor on-time performance.
news.why: Importers moving freight from Asia to the U.S. should expect hard space and unreliable schedules into late November, so they should book earlier and build extra transit buffer.

news.title: Canada Adjusts China Ties, Carney Says, Aiming To Clinch Right Deal with U.S.
news.summary: Canada is gradually re-engaging with China through a renewed currency swap, wider financial-sector access, expanded tariff relief for some farm and seafood exports, and a two-year extension of steel and aluminum remission measures.
news.why: Importers of Chinese steel or aluminum into Canada gain two more years of duty relief, while Canadian pork and seafood exporters get tariff cuts, so sourcing and pricing for those goods may shift.

news.title: Amazon’s first Puerto Rico delivery station speeds up shipping
news.summary: Amazon has opened a 100,000-square-foot delivery station in Puerto Rico that is expected to cut delivery times in the San Juan area from about two weeks to around two days.
news.why: Retailers and sellers serving Puerto Rico may gain faster local fulfillment options, which makes regional inventory placement worth reviewing.

news.title: Starbucks inventory availability at ‘all-time high’ with daily deliveries, CEO says
news.summary: Starbucks' CEO reports record inventory availability, which the company attributes partly to a test of 24-hour operations and more frequent deliveries.
news.why: The case shows that replenishment frequency and flexible operating hours can lift in-stock rates, a useful benchmark for retailers reviewing their own delivery cadence.

news.title: Survey: Profound Gap Between Knowing Supply Chain Risks and Acting on Them
news.summary: An Efficio survey of 400 business leaders finds most companies monitor critical risks, but only about half can quickly move resources when a disruption hits, with stronger performers far more likely to do so.
news.why: Supply chain managers should judge their risk programs by how fast they can reallocate suppliers and capacity, not only by how well they track threats.

news.title: PepsiCo improves deforestation-free sourcing for key commodities
news.summary: PepsiCo says 94% of its key ingredients, including palm oil and sugar cane, were sourced without forest clearance in 2025, up from 90% the year before.
news.why: Suppliers of commodity ingredients to large food brands face rising traceability expectations, so origin documentation is becoming a standard part of sourcing contracts.

news.title: Fashion brand nixes dedicated fulfillment model to boost transit times
news.summary: For Love & Lemons has moved its order fulfillment to a shared Cart.com facility in Texas to cut storage costs and speed deliveries.
news.why: Brands weighing dedicated versus shared fulfillment networks may find that a third-party hub lowers both storage cost and transit time.
